abstract: This Stanford study examines how artificial intelligence exposure is distributed across the labor market, finding that AI capabilities are concentrated among high-skill, high-wage occupations. However, the research indicates that wage and employment effects from AI adoption may not remain limited to these sectors but could cascade downward to affect lower-skill and lower-wage workers through competitive and structural labor market mechanisms.
keyFindings: AI exposure is concentrated among high-skill, high-wage occupations rather than distributed broadly across the labor market
Wage effects from AI adoption may cascade downward beyond the occupations with direct AI exposure
